req.title: Blog post title required on update
req.statement: The system shall reject POST /<id>/update with a missing title, rendering an error.
triggers: blog post title required on update

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update must reject requests with a missing title by rendering an error (HTTP 2xx with error content, not a redirect). We need: (1) a positive case where a valid title is provided and the update succeeds, (2) a negative case where title is empty string and the error is shown, (3) a boundary case where title is exactly one character (minimum non-empty). We also add a case where title key is omitted entirely. All tests use pre-loaded data: user Rahul (id=1) owns posts 2,3,6,8,9,10,11,12,15,18,19,20 — we use post id=2. Mutation resilience: assert exact status codes (200 vs 302), exact error text, and verify the database state is unchanged on failure.

tests.name: test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds
preconditions: User Rahul (id=1) is the author of post id=2
User is logged in as Rahul
actions: POST /2/update with title='Updated Title' and body='Updated body'
expected: Post title is updated in the database
trace: R-FLASKR-040: valid title accepted, redirect issued
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    r2 = client.get('/')
    assert b'Updated Title' in r2.data

test_update_with_valid_title_succeeds()

from flaskr import create_app

def test_update_with_empty_title_renders_error():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
